messages.subject: Calling for new developers for rapache
messages.subject_clean: Calling for new developers for rapache
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

If any of you are interested in helping with rapache, I'd be much
obliged. I've got two tasks that I'd like to accomplish:

1. Package up rapache for the various linux distributions, starting
with debian. I've tried several times in the past to learn how to
create a debian package, and honestly I just get confused and bored
every time. I think the way to aproach this task would be to dissect
one of the many libapache2-mod-* packages.

2. Port rapache to windows and "make it work". This will probably
involve a great deal of work as someone will need to mix and match
compiler tool chains between the apache build and the R build.

Also, if there are any other features you would like to add to
rapache, please let me know. I'm all ears!

Best,

Jeff

messages.subject: Preventing code injection
messages.body_plain:
I was wondering what kind of techniques other people use to prevent
code execution in rapache, or R scripts in general. For example, if I
have a web application with a string argument, how do I prevent
someone from inserting a shell() or exec() function as argument? Is
there a function in R similar to PHP's escapeshellarg() or
escapeshellcmd() ?

messages.subject: Re: Preventing code injection
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeroen,

Jeroen wrote on 07/29/2009 06:38 AM:
> I was wondering what kind of techniques other people use to prevent
> code execution in rapache, or R scripts in general. For example, if I
> have a web application with a string argument, how do I prevent
> someone from inserting a shell() or exec() function as argument? Is
> there a function in R similar to PHP's escapeshellarg() or
> escapeshellcmd() ?

Sadly, the best way to do it is to NOT pass user input directly into
another execution context, say SQL, shell, or even an eval in R. An
approximation is to match the user input with the set of all relevant
inputs the web application SHOULD accept. Once the match is made, then
the app can do what the user wanted.

In R, one can compute "on the language" which makes scrubbing user input
far worse. It's not just a matter of stripping out strings such as
system and exec from R code submitted by a user.

Those escape functions merely place the appropriate quotes, double
quotes, and backticks around strings.

Jeff
